name: @pipeworx/mcp-uniprot

tools.name: search
tools.description: "Find protein [name]" / "look up [gene] in UniProt" / "BRCA1 / TP53 / insulin protein info" / "all proteins for [organism]" — UniProtKB search via Lucene-style queries (e.g. gene:BRCA1 AND organism_id:9606 for human BRCA1). UniProt is the authoritative protein-sequence-and-function database — use for protein characterization, function annotation, sequence retrieval, and cross-references to PDB/GO/PubMed.

query.description: Lucene-style expression, passed bare — do NOT wrap the whole thing in quotes. Fielded terms combine with AND, e.g. gene:BRCA1 AND organism_id:9606. Quotes are only for a multi-word value, e.g. organism_name:"Homo sapiens". Plain-English questions match poorly because every token must appear; prefer keywords.

tools.name: get
tools.description: "Fetch protein [P12345]" / "UniProt entry for [accession]" / "FASTA sequence for [protein]" — single UniProtKB entry by accession (e.g. P12345 or P38398 for BRCA1_HUMAN). Returns full protein record: sequence, function annotations, GO terms, cross-refs, post-translational modifications, variants. Pass format=fasta for sequence only.

tools.name: proteomes_search
tools.description: "Reference proteome for [organism]" / "complete protein set of [species]" — search UniProt reference proteomes (the curated representative protein set per organism). Use as a starting point for genome-scale protein analyses.

tools.name: taxonomy_search
tools.description: "NCBI taxonomy ID for [organism]" / "taxid for [species]" / "look up [Latin name] in NCBI taxonomy" — search NCBI Taxonomy via UniProt's mirror. Returns taxonomic IDs you can use as organism_id filters in `search` (9606 = human, 10090 = mouse, 7227 = D. melanogaster, etc).

tools.name: keyword
tools.description: "UniProt keyword KW-N info" / "what does keyword [X] mean" — fetch a UniProt controlled-vocabulary keyword by ID. Use to look up annotation tags like "Kinase" / "Membrane" / "Disease-associated".

tools.name: feature_summary
tools.description: "Domain map of [protein]" / "annotated features of [accession]" / "what regions / sites does [protein] have" — annotated features (domains, active sites, transmembrane regions, mutagenesis sites, glycosylation, disulfide bonds, etc.) for a UniProt accession. Use for structural/functional analysis without pulling the full protein record.

instructions: @pipeworx/mcp-uniprot forwards to the Pipeworx gateway and lists only the uniprot pack's tools. Set PIPEWORX_META_TOOLS=1 to also list ask_pipeworx and the other gateway-wide tools.
